public_rationale: The accessible records do not establish either the predominant coverage pattern or the claim that only a small fraction of AI investments had come online. Microsoft reported monetizing new capacity, while MoneyWeek described differing investor reactions. These are material qualifications, but neither supplies the group-wide deployment fraction or representative coverage sample needed to support or contradict the full claim.
limitations: Revenue-producing additions can coexist with substantial unfinished investment.
A few examples cannot establish what investors and commentators said for the most part.
The deployment threshold and investment denominator remain imprecise.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hyperscalers have mostly been credited for their capex because overall revenues grew, with everyone saying their 'AI bets have paid off', when it is clear those AI bets have barely started to come online.

statement.excerpt: For the most part, hyperscalers have been given credit for their capital expenditures because overall revenues have grown, with everyone saying that their “AI bets have paid off,” when it’s clear that the AI bets in question have barely started to come online.

from_speaker: given credit for their capital expenditures because overall revenues have grown
everyone saying that their “AI bets have paid off”
our_interpretation: 'Everyone' is ordinary rhetorical emphasis, not a claim about every commentator.
'For the most part' describes a predominant pattern of investor and press interpretation; it is not a conditional forecast antecedent.
'Barely started' means only a small fraction of the AI infrastructure investment cohort discussed since 2022 had become operational.
Hyperscalers means Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta.

For the ongoing deployment state, I use April through June 2026, the latest completed quarterly period publicly reportable before publication. Subsequent pre-post coverage of those results is context for the claimed narrative.
The core test concerns deployment and how it was represented, not a separately specified revenue or capex amount.
criteria.support_condition: Representative coverage predominantly credits revenue growth to the AI investment program, while comparable commissioning records establish that only a small fraction of that investment cohort was operational in the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative coverage does not show the claimed predominant attribution, or comparable deployment records establish that a substantial share of the relevant AI investment cohort was already operational.
